chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara, who said:

Abu Ja' Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'When you recite the Adhan, be eloquent with the Alif and the Ha, and send blessings upon the Prophet every time you mention him, or when a reciter mentions him during the Adhan or otherwise.'

key_terms.أَذَّنْتَ: You recite the Adhan (call to prayer)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on pronouncing letters and sending blessings during the Adhan?
ai.summary: Imam Abu Ja'far (asws) emphasizes the aesthetic and spiritual precision of the Adhan by instructing the reciter to articulate the vowels 'Alif' and 'Ha' with clarity, enhancing the melodic resonance of the call. Furthermore, he mandates the inclusion of Salawat upon the Prophet (saww) whenever his name is invoked, linking the act of calling to prayer with the perpetual remembrance of the Prophet's status. This instruction underscores the Shia emphasis on the beauty of worship and the integral connection between the Adhan and the Prophet's legacy.
